title: shadowboard-14d-rotation-and-skill-delegation-notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, runnable plan for a 14-day "shadowboard" rotation: a candidate or internal hire trial where they rotate across 3 small pods to validate cross-functional fit and accelerate an evidence-backed hiring decision. It combines pairing, small deliverables, and rapid feedback loops so hiring decisions are based on observed collaboration, troubleshooting, and handoff ability rather than just whiteboard performance.

When to use this instead of a long take-home or extended onsite:
- Role requires cross-team collaboration and operational handoffs (platform, SRE, product integration, solutions engineering).
- Need to evaluate communication, autonomy, and ramp speed in a real-team context.
- Hiring on a tight timeline and want observable signals in production-like tasks.

High-level schedule (14 days):
- Day 0 (pre-rotation): access checklist, reading packet, welcome note from host manager, calendar invites for syncs.
- Days 1–3: Pod A (infra/platform) — orientation, pair on a small bug or infra observation, deliver a 30–60 min findings doc + action items.
- Days 4–6: Pod B (product/integration) — work on a tiny story or QA triage, own one PR or test case.
- Days 7–9: Pod C (customer-facing / solutions) — shadow a support incident or write a short runbook.
- Days 10–11: Cross-pod handoff exercise — take the artifacts from other pods and draft a consolidated handoff + prioritization recommendation.
- Day 12: Behavioral review / structured interview debrief (30–45m).
- Day 13: Hiring panel — 45m triage + 30m decision sync with hiring manager and panelists.
- Day 14: Final report (candidate and host feedback) + decision deliverable.

Goals and success signals (what we are explicitly scoring):
- Technical correctness (does work meet basic quality, tests, and guidelines?) — weight 30%
- Communication clarity (handoff notes, Slack threads, in-call explanations) — weight 25%
- Prioritization & impact sense (did they pick the right scope to deliver?) — weight 20%
- Autonomy & ramp speed (how much support was required?) — weight 15%
- Culture fit / collaboration (engagement, code review conduct, receptive to feedback) — weight 10%

Quick rubric (one-page summary for panelists):
- 4 (Exceeds): completes deliverable with minimal guidance, clear rationale, proactive follow-up, writing that scales to other teams.
- 3 (Meets): finishes expected scope, needs occasional clarifying questions, clean handoff.
- 2 (Marginal): partial completion, significant follow-ups required, ambiguity persists.
- 1 (Insufficient): deliverable not usable, repeated blocking without ownership.

Artifacts we collect (minimum):
- One short PR or patch with reviewer comments (link).
- A 1-page findings note (markdown) from Pod A.
- A runbook draft or incident postmortem snippet from Pod C.
- Candidate final one-page reflection (what they learned, what they'd change).
- Panel scorings and verbatim feedback snippets (consolidated).

Logistics & risk mitigation (operational notes):
- Access: ensure GitHub readonly + a test environment sandbox by Day 0. If customer data is required, use synthetic fixtures.
- Time commitment: pods should schedule 2–3 hours/day of active pairing or check-ins; avoid full-day immersion for engineers who are shipping.
- Compensation: paid trial or contractor stipend for external candidates (recommendation: 2–3 days' equivalent pay pro-rated).
- Confidentiality: candidate signs a short NDA for working with internal artifacts if necessary.

Week-one onboarding-lite checklist (for hosts):
- Pre-rotation (People Ops): create calendar invites, Slack channel, add to repo, confirm sandbox.
- Day 0 (Host manager): 30m welcome + role overview, success signals, how to escalate blockers.
- Day 1 morning (Pod lead): 15m micro-orientation + 90m pairing session.
- Daily stand (10m): quick sync on blockers and plan.
- Mid-pod check (end of Day 3 & Day 6): 30m feedback touchpoint.

Feedback cadence and templates:
- After each pod (Day 3, Day 6, Day 9): host completes quick rubric (one line + 3 bullet examples).
- End-of-rotation panel: each panelist submits final score (1–4) for each success signal and 2–3 supporting sentences.
- Candidate feedback loop: schedule a 30m wrap for candidate to share reflection + give/receive feedback.

Decision matrix (sample):
- Hire: average rubric score >= 3.4 AND hiring manager confidence >= 80% AND at least one artifact with accepted PR.
- Consider for further interview: average 2.6–3.4 with specific remediation plan (30–60 day onboarding goals).
- No-hire: average < 2.6 OR major safety/security or code-of-conduct red flags.

Sample panel assignment (who to invite):
- Hiring manager (final lead) — required.
- Two cross-functional peers who worked with candidate during rotation (Pod A/B lead).
- One engineering manager from adjacent team (for org fit).
- People Ops coordinator (to document decision & next steps).

Template messages (paste-ready):
- Welcome note to candidate: "Hi {name}, welcome to Redwood's 14-day shadowboard. Attached is a one-page role brief, access details, and our success signals. Your first day is {date}. We'll pair you with {Pod A lead} — expect a 90m pairing with a small starter task."
- Panel invite (short): "Please join an evidence review for {candidate} on {date}. We will use a 45m timebox to review artifacts and scores — bring brief examples from your pod."

Open questions / decisions to finalize before running widely:
- Stipend amount for external candidates (finance/people ops to confirm).
- Standard synthetic fixture repo (infra to provide).
- Legal clarifications for candidate-created artifacts and IP (legal).

Next steps (for People Ops):
- Pilot two rotations in Q4: one IC same-team internal transfer, one external candidate paid trial.
- Capture 10 signal mappings post-pilot: which micro-tasks were most predictive of 30/90 day success.
- Build a short training for pod leads (15–20m) on giving structured feedback quickly.

Notes to self (Maya):
- Keep trial low-friction for hosts — cap pairing time and provide clear micro-tasks so reviewers don't need to invent work.
- Track conversion and first-90-day ramp metrics for hires who came through Shadowboard and compare to baseline hires.

Attachments (to produce before pilot):
- 1-page role brief template (md)
- One-line rubric form (Google Form template)
- Stipend approval workflow

End of doc.
